description: Node/TypeScript ecosystem groupings — peer-dep coupled families that must move together.

toolSettings.description: Cap (MB) for the pnpm/yarn child process Renovate spawns to refresh lockfiles — the usual OOM culprit on Mend-hosted, where NODE_OPTIONS can't be set. 2560 = 2.5GiB; Mend imposes no max beyond the plan, so raise toward that ceiling if runs still OOM. Requires renovate ≥ the version pinned in validate.yml. https://docs.renovatebot.com/mend-hosted/faq/

packageRules.description: React core + types
TanStack libraries (router/query/table share majors)
Radix UI primitives (shadcn/ui)
Vite + plugins (plugin majors track Vite majors)

Tailwind v4 engine + first-party plugins. `tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/vite` ship from the tailwindlabs monorepo in exact lockstep (both 4.3.3 in owine/youth-activity-scheduler) and the plugin drives the engine's internal API rather than a stable public one, so a split major is a guaranteed break, not a drift risk. Membership is deliberately narrow. Everything under `@tailwindcss/*` (vite, postcss, cli) is first-party and moves with the engine, but `tailwind-merge` and `tw-animate-css` are THIRD-PARTY and independently released — which is why this is `tailwindcss` plus the scope regex and NOT a `/^tailwind/` regex: that would wrongly swallow `tailwind-merge` and hold a Tailwind major hostage to an unrelated maintainer's cadence. MAJORS ride the group on purpose (no `matchUpdateTypes`), same reasoning as the `testing` rule below.

Vitest stack (engine + every @vitest/* package + testcontainers + vite peer). Scope regex, NOT an allowlist: the previous list named `@vitest/coverage-v8` only, so `@vitest/ui` belonged to no group at all and a single v4->v5 upgrade split into two PRs that were each green in CI and each broken in use — owine/youth-activity-scheduler #421 (vitest 4.1.11 -> 5.0.0, which rode this group's branch as a one-member group, hence the single-dep PR title) and #420 (@vitest/ui 4.1.11 -> 5.0.0, on its own branch). `@vitest/ui` declares an EXACT `vitest` peer, but pnpm 12 warns rather than fails on an unmet peer and resolves `@vitest/ui@4.1.11(vitest@5.0.0)` anyway; `vitest --ui` then dies at startup with `Loaded vitest@5.0.0 and @vitest/ui@4.1.11. Running mixed versions is not supported` followed by `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'uiBase')`. No CI script passes `--ui`, so install/test/typecheck/lint all passed on both halves and nothing caught it. #420 is the mirror image (v5 UI inside a v4 runner). The fix is the scope regex rather than one more name: a missing group member raises no error anywhere — it just quietly produces a second PR — so there is no signal separating "correctly ungrouped" from "silently fell out", and an allowlist is exactly what failed here. `/^@vitest//` also picks up `@vitest/browser` and anything else published under the scope. Same hazard documented on docker.json's `github-actions-setup` rule, which remains an allowlist because GitHub Actions have no shared scope to match on. MAJORS: intentionally no `matchUpdateTypes` — the group applies to majors too, which is the whole point, since the break is a major skew. Per the `python runtime` precedent in python.json, grouping decides which deps share a branch, not how it is reviewed: default.json's separateMajorMinor/separateMultipleMajor still isolate the major, and its major rule still applies the 7-day soak, `automerge: false`, `feat:`, and `major-update`/`needs-review` labels.

React Testing Library + its DOM engine. `@testing-library/react` declares a real peer on `@testing-library/dom` (^10) and consumers install the DOM package directly, so the two must cross a major on the same branch or the renderer and the query engine disagree about the DOM API. Deliberately an explicit PAIR, not the `/^@testing-library//` scope regex used for @vitest above: the rest of this neighborhood — `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `@testing-library/user-event`, plus `happy-dom` and `msw` — is INDEPENDENTLY released and shares no version line (7.0.1 / 14.6.7 / 20.14.3 / 2.15.0 in owine/youth-activity-scheduler). Grouping those would be churn reduction, which is a legitimate goal but a different and weaker justification than break prevention, and it would block a genuine peer-pair upgrade behind an unrelated maintainer's release cadence. The scope regex is right for @vitest (one monorepo, one version line) and wrong here; the distinction is the release train, not the naming.
ESLint plugins + typescript-eslint. The bare `typescript-eslint` meta-package is unscoped, so the /^@typescript-eslint// regex never matched it — it must be listed explicitly.

ESLint core + `@eslint/js`. The two are published from the eslint monorepo at the same version on every release, and flat configs import `@eslint/js` for its recommended rule set, so a skew runs one release's rule catalog against another release's engine. Neither could ever have been caught by the `eslint plugins` rule above: that matches `/^eslint-/`, and a scope prefix moves the string start, so the regex cannot match `@eslint/js` by construction — the same class of miss as the bare `typescript-eslint` meta-package noted on that rule. owine/youth-activity-scheduler has already drifted to eslint 10.10.0 against @eslint/js 10.0.1. DELIBERATELY its own group rather than folding the core into `eslint plugins`: plugins carry a peer range on eslint's major, so bundling would put an eslint major AND every plugin's compatibility bump on one branch — an un-reviewable diff that cannot land until the slowest plugin publishes — and renaming `eslint plugins` to cover the core would churn branch names in every consumer for no correctness gain. Named explicitly, NOT `/^@eslint//`: `@eslint/css`, `@eslint/json`, and `@eslint/markdown` are separately-released plugins that merely share the scope, so the scope regex would recreate the bundling this rule avoids (contrast the @vitest rule above, where the whole scope IS one release train). ACCEPTED TRADEOFF: on an eslint major, plugin compat bumps land in a separate PR. That is tolerable here in a way the @vitest/ui split was not — plugins declare a peer RANGE and generally still load across a core major, whereas `@vitest/ui` pins an exact version and hard-asserts on mismatch at startup. Residual risk, not zero risk; the major rule's `needs-review` label is the backstop.

Next.js core + first-party plugins + `eslint-config-next`. The config is version-locked to the framework (16.3.5 ships against next 16.x) rather than peer-ranged — its declared `eslint` peer is a loose `>=9.0.0`, so nothing in the resolver stops a stale config sitting against a new Next major while silently missing that major's lint rules. MUST stay ordered AFTER the `eslint plugins` rule above: `eslint-config-next` matches that rule's `/^eslint-/`, and last matching rule wins, so moving this rule earlier would hand the config back to `eslint plugins` and re-split it from the framework it tracks.

Playwright npm family — the runner, the driver, and the a11y binding all ride one release train. `@axe-core/playwright` peers on `playwright-core` (`>= 1.0.0`), and `@playwright/test` bundles a driver whose version must match the browser binaries installed by `playwright install`, so a split major leaves the runner and its browsers disagreeing. SCOPED TO `matchDatasources: [npm]` AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATION: PyPI publishes a `playwright` package under the identical name, and owine/youth-activity-scheduler extends BOTH :node and :python, so an unscoped rule here would reach across into pep621 and build the cross-manager group that was deliberately DECLINED in #90 (separate browser-binary installs, separate purposes, and grouping across two registries means neither half lands until both publish). Deliberately named `playwright` to match the pre-existing repo-local rule in owine/house-manager, which adds `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright` to the same group name — a docker-image coupling that is real in that repo only and correctly stays repo-local. Identical group names merge rather than fight, so that rule keeps working unchanged.

react-hook-form + its resolver adapters — `@hookform/resolvers` declares a hard peer on `react-hook-form` (^7.55.0) and re-exports its types, so a major skew is a type-level break. `zod` is INTENTIONALLY NOT HERE despite also being a declared peer of the resolvers package: zod is a standalone validator used by six fleet repos that have no forms layer at all (the MCP servers, doc-scanner/server, house-manager), so grouping it would drag an unrelated major into every forms PR and vice versa. The resolvers package peers on ~25 validators; following that peer list into groupings would collapse half of npm into one branch.

Stylelint + its shareable configs — `stylelint-config-standard` declares a hard `stylelint` peer (^17.0.0) and configs are cut per stylelint major, so a split major fails the lint run outright rather than degrading. Mirrors the `eslint` / `eslint plugins` split above in shape, but is deliberately ONE group rather than two: the stylelint config ecosystem is a short chain (standard -> recommended) rather than eslint's broad plugin surface, so there is no un-reviewable-diff hazard to separate for.

tesseract.js + its wasm core — `tesseract.js` carries `tesseract.js-core` as a caret dependency (^7.0.0), and doc-scanner/pwa installs BOTH directly so it can control the wasm asset path. Direct-installing a transitive is what creates the hazard: on a split major the JS wrapper resolves its own nested core while the app loads the hoisted one, giving two wasm runtimes. Not a peer declaration, so nothing warns.

Sentry SDKs — every `@sentry/*` package is published from one monorepo at one version, and the platform packages (`@sentry/node`, `@sentry/nextjs`) share a `@sentry/core` singleton that throws on a version mismatch at init. Whole-scope regex is correct here for the same reason it is correct for `@vitest/*` and wrong for `@eslint/*`: the scope IS the release train, with no third-party publishers inside it.

TypeScript compiler family — TypeScript 7 (the Go port) ships no JS API, so tools needing programmatic compiler access (typescript-eslint, Next.js) require the `@typescript/typescript6` compat package aliased over the `typescript` specifier while a second alias supplies the v7 `tsc` bin. Group them so the side-by-side aliases move coherently. https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10940 — see also the "Running side-by-side with TypeScript 6.0" section of https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/
Prisma — client + adapter + CLI must bump together
Auth.js — peer-dep coupled
pg + types
Hono + middleware/plugin ecosystem
Preact core + plugins
Cloudflare Workers toolchain — wrangler + workers-types + workers SDKs travel together

PRE-SEEDED, NOT YET IN THE FLEET. The rules from here to the end of this block cover ecosystems no owine repo installs today; they exist so that the FIRST repo to adopt one is grouped correctly on day one rather than discovering the split the way owine/youth-activity-scheduler#420/#421 did. A rule that matches nothing costs nothing at resolve time, and this preset already carries forward-looking entries on the same logic (see the node-lts-26 lane at the bottom of this file). Each is a single scope or release train verified to publish in lockstep; the soft ones are labelled as churn reduction rather than break prevention so a future reader does not mistake the justification. Storybook: every @storybook/* package is one monorepo release and the framework/builder/addon triple asserts on mismatch at boot.

PRE-SEEDED. OpenTelemetry JS — the API/SDK/instrumentation packages share a registered global and silently no-op (or throw) across a version boundary; the canonical example of a family that must move as one. NAME SUFFIXED `-js` ON PURPOSE: python.json has its own `opentelemetry-python` group, and identical group names would put both ecosystems' OTel updates on one branch in any repo extending :node and :python. See the `aws-sdk-js` rule above for the full reasoning.

PRE-SEEDED. AWS SDK v3 for JS — one monorepo, one version, and clients share middleware/signing internals across packages. Deliberately excludes `/^@smithy//`: it is the separately-versioned runtime layer beneath the SDK, so folding it in would couple two release trains that are only range-compatible. NAME SUFFIXED `-js` ON PURPOSE — do NOT 'tidy' it back to a bare `aws-sdk`. python.json groups boto3/botocore, and a groupName is a BRANCH name: two rules sharing one name share one PR regardless of which manager or file they came from. Since youth-activity-scheduler and claude-terminal-home-assistant extend BOTH :node and :python, a shared name would merge unrelated @aws-sdk/* and boto3 updates into one cross-manager PR — the same coupling explicitly declined for playwright in #90, arrived at through group names instead of package matching. (That name-merging behaviour is load-bearing elsewhere and deliberate: the `playwright` group above shares its name with a repo-local rule in owine/house-manager so the two combine. Same mechanism, opposite intent — which is exactly why it has to be chosen, not inherited.)
PRE-SEEDED. tRPC — client/server/adapters are strictly lockstep and the wire contract is not stable across majors.

PRE-SEEDED. Drizzle — `drizzle-kit` reads schema files against `drizzle-orm` internals, so a skew breaks migration generation rather than the app, which means CI on the app side can pass while `drizzle-kit generate` is broken. Same silent-on-CI shape as the @vitest/ui break.
PRE-SEEDED. NestJS — core/common/platform packages are one release train with peer ranges on each other.
PRE-SEEDED. Babel — @babel/core and its presets/plugins share internal AST contracts across one monorepo release.
PRE-SEEDED. SWC — @swc/core and its bindings/helpers are version-matched, and the native binding is compiled against a specific core.

PRE-SEEDED. Jest family — jest, its @jest/* internals, and the transform/environment adapters (`ts-jest`, `babel-jest`, `jest-environment-jsdom`) are cut per jest major and peer on it. Listed explicitly rather than by a `/^jest-/` regex, which would sweep in unrelated third-party `jest-*` matchers and reporters that are not lockstep.

PRE-SEEDED. Astro + first-party integrations. CHURN REDUCTION more than break prevention: @astrojs/* integrations are separately versioned and peer-ranged on astro rather than lockstep, so a split is usually survivable — grouped because an Astro major reliably drags every integration with it and reviewing them apart is noise.
PRE-SEEDED. Nuxt + @nuxt/kit + @nuxt/schema — these ARE lockstep with the framework release (unlike the Astro case above), and modules resolve @nuxt/kit at build time.

PRE-SEEDED. SvelteKit + adapters + the vite plugin. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES bare `svelte`: the compiler and SvelteKit are SEPARATE release trains (svelte 5 vs kit 2), so grouping them would force two unrelated majors onto one branch. The @sveltejs/* scope alone is the real lockstep unit — adapters peer on kit's major. Pre-seeding a wrong grouping is worse than pre-seeding none, which is why this one is scope-only.
PRE-SEEDED. Expo SDK — `expo` and the `expo-*` modules are released as one numbered SDK; mixing module versions across an SDK line is explicitly unsupported upstream.

PRE-SEEDED. Apollo + graphql. CHURN REDUCTION: @apollo/* packages peer on `graphql` as a wide range rather than pinning it, so a split rarely breaks — grouped because a graphql major is the thing that forces the Apollo bump, and seeing them apart hides that causality.

PRE-SEEDED. Clerk SDKs. CHURN REDUCTION: @clerk/* packages share a backend API contract and are usually released together, but the framework bindings carry independent version lines, so this prevents PR noise rather than a guaranteed break.

PRE-SEEDED. Supabase SDKs. CHURN REDUCTION, same shape as the Clerk rule: supabase-js bundles the sub-clients (postgrest/realtime/storage/gotrue) as regular dependencies, so direct-installing several of them is the only way a skew appears — and when it does it behaves like the tesseract.js-core case above rather than a hard peer failure.

Node + pnpm toolchain — engines, packageManager, .nvmrc, Dockerfile `FROM node:X`, and the Dockerfile `ARG PNPM_VERSION` custom manager all move in lockstep. A repo with engineStrict CANNOT build with these split: the Dockerfile pins one Node and package.json demands another, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE on BOTH halves and neither PR can go green alone. The lockstep is only real because docker.json's `dockerfile bases` rule negates these same names — it matches `matchManagers: [dockerfile]` and consumers extend `:node` before `:docker`, so the later preset would otherwise win the groupName and pull `FROM node:X` out. Keep this list and that negation in sync. (`ARG PNPM_VERSION` needs no carve-out there: it is a `custom.regex` manager, not `dockerfile`, so `dockerfile bases` never matched it — it reaches this group via its `pnpm` depNameTemplate.) The fully-qualified `docker.io/library/node` form is listed because `FROM docker.io/library/node:X` yields that depName rather than the bare `node`; it is a plain string (glob-matched, `.`/`/` literal) so it matches exactly and does not catch `nodered/node-red` or the like.

Per-LTS-lane Node slots — workflow matrix entries annotated with `depName=node-lts-NN packageName=node` represent a specific LTS line and must not be major-bumped. Listed lanes cover current + near-future LTSs; add a new entry when a new LTS ships.
